parent_title: Spec: evidence-backed AI/ML research question discovery

tickets.title: Persist private Research Projects on the supplied starter
tickets.deliver: An authenticated researcher can create a private project, save and revise a research brief, rename/archive it, and return to the saved project list. Reconcile the existing starter in this first usable path rather than regenerating it.
criteria: Reuse the existing Next.js/Hono/tRPC/Better Auth/shared UI wiring and pnpm/Varlock conventions. Keep native scaffolding compiling without adding mobile features. Read the installed Next.js guidance before changing web code.

Introduce project ownership, active/archived/deleting states, brief revision history, and input bounds from the spec. Incomplete briefs save; discovery requires a title and topic. Unknown resources are recorded as unknown.

The project list and overview replace research-facing starter demo navigation and support create, read, edit, archive/unarchive, and safe deletion of projects containing only this slice’s data. Provide tombstone/access and cleanup registration contracts for later artifacts; no future data tables.

Introduce one shared project mutation guard: archived projects permit reads and unarchive but reject other writes; deleting projects deny access/publication. Every later manual/API/worker mutation uses this guard. Test archived brief changes and cross-account unarchive attempts. No live pilot is enabled by this first slice.

Use a transaction-capable Node PostgreSQL connection and Drizzle adapter in place of the current Neon HTTP-only application connection, preserving Neon as the database host and the auth relations adapter. Keep pool lifetimes bounded for serverless API requests and persistent workers; separate migration/worker connection settings where required. Verify rollback against disposable PostgreSQL.
Separate the importable Hono application from socket-listening bootstrap and inject application services so tests can exercise requests without starting a server or loading production secrets.

Introduce Vitest API integration fixtures with a real disposable PostgreSQL database and a small Playwright project-flow check. Two accounts cannot list/read/change/delete each other’s projects; missing and unauthorized IDs have indistinguishable not-found responses.
Optimistic concurrency prevents one tab overwriting another brief revision. Keyboard forms, labelled validation errors, and 360px/1280px layouts preserve unsaved input.

Record the supplied baseline and fix the observed formatter differences as a separate mechanical commit before functional changes; use non-mutating checks for verification. Typechecking and formatting of the resulting touched code pass.

tickets.title: Restrict Research Projects to invited verified pilot accounts
tickets.deliver: An invited researcher can register, verify email, sign in, recover access, and open their projects; uninvited, unverified, and revoked accounts see actionable access states and cannot use research APIs.
criteria: Extend the existing Better Auth instance and email/password forms with verified-email enforcement, verification/recovery delivery adapters, and a normalized invited-email policy enforced by the backend, not only navigation.

An authenticated operator configuration/administrative mechanism adds/revokes eligibility with actor/time/email/reason audit records. Provide a runbook and deterministic mail-delivery fixtures; there is no public allowlist-management endpoint or invitation administration UI.

Revocation immediately denies new research operations and exposes a stable eligibility check that future workers use to cancel that account’s work. Preserve private projects unless separately deleted; later job slices implement cancellation against this policy.

Verification, pending eligibility, expired links, recovery, sign-out, and rejected access have usable web states without leaking account existence in recovery responses. A signup does not automatically bypass verification by redirecting to the dashboard.

Preserve same-origin deployed /api routing, direct local API access, SSR cookie forwarding, and existing native auth compatibility. Validate development and production cookie/origin/CSRF settings instead of assuming the current Secure/SameSite=None defaults work everywhere.

API tests deny uninvited/unverified/revoked sessions even with guessed project IDs. Fixture-backed browser checks cover sign-in/verification/recovery and authenticated project return. Live mail delivery remains disabled until configured and verified; no test mail is sent to real people by default.

tickets.title: Run resumable scoped literature searches with spending limits
tickets.deliver: A researcher edits a Literature Scope, submits a fixture-backed search, sees a durable job and dated results, leaves the page, and returns to accurate progress and coverage. Budget and cancellation behavior are delivered with the first queued operation.
criteria: Provide editable one-to-three search queries, exact source choices/filters, criteria, recent-five-year default and older-foundation intent. Query templates are deterministic; the UI confirms the exact queries transmitted, never extra private brief fields.

Persist scope/brief revisions, immutable Literature Snapshots and per-source outcomes/cursors/counts/cache ages/truncation. Initial deterministic provider fixtures produce papers and success/empty/partial/failed outcomes without paid calls.

Introduce a separately runnable Node worker and pg-boss coordination with the application write and enqueue on the same PostgreSQL transaction. Use the existing Node stack; polling workers do not run inside Vercel request handlers.

Persist queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled stages, checkpoints and idempotency keys. Repeated identical submissions return the existing job; changed input with the same key conflicts. Five-second visible-page polling/backoff/refocus restores state.

Enforce two active runs per account and two executing runs globally; safe retrieval retries have at most three total attempts. Check project tombstone/archive and account revocation before dispatch and publication. A restart or cancelled/deleted job cannot duplicate or resurrect results.

Deliver usage reservations and visible budget status now: $1/run, $5/project/month, $50/global/month, UTC months, pending-reservation-aware atomic limits and measured reconciliation. Metered source/model attempts and retries use this shared mechanism; unknown pricing disables paid routes while free fixtures/manual work remain available.

Test transaction rollback with no orphaned queue entry, restarted workers, duplicate submissions, cancellation/revocation, partial coverage, concurrent reservations, monthly rollover and unknown-pricing rejection. Simulate uncertain paid outcomes conservatively without automatic paid retry.

Register snapshot/job/reservation lifecycle cleanup with project deletion and redact private queries/content from job lists and diagnostics. Document distinct API/worker/migration environment schemas, worker packaging and database connectivity; local servers still require permission.

tickets.title: Discover literature and foundational work through OpenAlex
tickets.deliver: A researcher runs the saved scope against OpenAlex and can inspect real paper results, source coverage, and deliberately included older foundational work without changing the durable workflow.
criteria: Implement an OpenAlex adapter over the existing fixture contract, with configured credentials/quotas, effective query/filter provenance, pagination, allowed caching, provider metadata/aliases and source dates. Keep credentials server-only.

Retrieve a bounded initial collection and citation/direct-lookup foundation expansion; older papers explicitly record the acquisition reason. Reserve capacity for the later arXiv/status stages and persist actual provider allocations within the 200-record discovery cap.

Handle missing supported filters, timeouts, 429/rate headers, stale cache, empty response, and partial cursor completion through existing source outcomes. Global provider throttling respects the deployment-wide quota; a failure is never a successful empty corpus.

Reconcile exact stable identifiers without automatically merging fuzzy title matches. Show paper titles, identifiers, source links, dates, preprint status when supplied, and metadata/abstract evidence availability; no automatic PDF download is introduced here.
Every paid route and retry goes through the shared atomic reservation ledger before execution. Unconfigured price/quota information disables only that route and preserves saved searches/results.

Extend fixture API/browser checks for live-adapter-shaped data, truncation, source failure, older work and cache age. Add an explicitly invoked live smoke check/runbook without consuming paid quota or creating live accounts during ordinary tests.

tickets.title: Add arXiv freshness and Crossref publication-status reconciliation
tickets.deliver: A researcher sees recent arXiv work alongside broader discovery, with DOI/preprint/version relationships and known corrections, withdrawals or retractions retained rather than silently merged.
criteria: Add arXiv metadata search/version refresh and Crossref DOI/status reconciliation behind the existing literature adapters. Preserve each effective query, dates, provider outcome, source freshness and uncertainty.

Allocate the existing 200-record cap across OpenAlex/arXiv/foundation work, deduplicating exact stable IDs while retaining per-source provenance. DOI/arXiv/provider aliases and related versions do not replace the text/version previously inspected.

Honor arXiv deployment-wide connection/rate restrictions and all connector quota/backoff controls. Failed reconciliation marks status unknown/incomplete without claiming clearance. Semantic Scholar remains disabled.

Expose known retractions/withdrawals, corrections and last-checked information in saved results. Flag disallowed positive support and emit/version a status change for later reviews to observe; historical snapshots are not silently rewritten.

Ambiguous similarity matches remain separate with reviewable possible-match information. User-confirmed reconciliation preserves original IDs, version links and membership/provenance history; title alone cannot force a merge.

API/browser fixtures cover DOI/preprint duplicates, fuzzy ambiguity, newer versions, retracted/corrected sources, failed lookup and shared throttling. Live credentials/terms/status coverage checks remain separately invoked and recorded.

tickets.title: Screen and search a versioned Literature Snapshot
tickets.deliver: A researcher can browse, search, filter, include, exclude and inspect the provenance of discovered papers while preserving the screening decisions used by later gap investigations.
criteria: Add paginated full-text metadata search and year/provider/screening/evidence/publication-status filters to the project library. Each row distinguishes metadata-only, permitted abstract and full-text availability and retains its source/version links.

Snapshot membership starts undecided. Including/excluding creates append-only screening revisions; exclusion requires a reason. Only included records can support generation. Preserve reasons when reopened or when related paper versions are reconciled.

Expose per-source success/empty/partial/failure, effective filters, source dates/cache ages, records actually inspected and truncation. New searches create new immutable snapshots, and promoting an investigation snapshot is an explicit action.
Provide ownership-checked membership/source reading and expected-revision edits. Cross-project IDs fail generically; conflicting edits retain the user’s unsaved reason/selection.

Add a library selection/version footprint and invalidation signal consumed by later candidates/reviews. A historical snapshot and its screening revision remain inspectable without relabelling old evidence as current.

Test API provenance/screening history, undecided-record rejection at the evidence contract, pagination, filter correctness, conflict and isolation. Browser-check keyboard screening, empty/partial states and long titles/excerpts at the required widths.

Register membership/revision data with project cleanup. Known status fields can arrive through fixtures and later source reconciliation; do not make arXiv/Crossref completion an unnecessary blocker for this library slice.

tickets.title: Inspect private PDF evidence and verify Evidence Anchors
tickets.deliver: A researcher uploads an authorized text PDF for a project paper, sees privately extracted page-linked passages, and verifies/corrects anchors before using them as support. Abstract evidence remains distinguishable and inspectable.
criteria: Add rights/processing-purpose capture and a separate private-content model consent record; uploading or parsing does not imply permission for a model call. Unknown permissions remain metadata/source-link only.

Use project-owned private S3 keys and signed upload/download issuance with five-minute expiry. Completion verifies actual size, PDF signature/type, checksum and ownership; default limits are 30 MB/100 pages and 20 accepted full-text documents per run.

Queue bounded PDF.js parsing through the durable worker. Retain document/source versions, content hashes, extraction versions, pages/spans/context and low-quality/table ambiguity. Scan/garbled/low-text content is needs-review; do not invent OCR or reliable table facts.

Show the permitted source document and contextual excerpt alongside abstract/full-text evidence labels. Researchers can create/correct/verify anchors; changed quotations create revisions. Unmatched corrections remain user notes, not trusted source quotes.

Abstract anchors reference permitted provider/version text and a real text locator without fictitious pages. Ownership and project-source relationships are enforced for anchor creation, reading, verification and signed access.

Input documents cannot change parser/model/tool permissions. Bound parser resources/time and protect MIME/content handling. Repeated parsing yields the same versioned checkpoint; cancellation/archive/revocation/tombstones prevent late anchors.

Deliver private-file/extraction/anchor cleanup registration, 24-hour abandoned-upload cleanup, and an error/status view. Fixture tests cover oversize/mismatched uploads, private URLs, corrupted/scanned/table-heavy PDFs, locator/quote corrections, cross-project IDs and deletion races.
Keyboard source inspection and correction preserve unsaved input. Live S3/parser fidelity remains a recorded enablement gate, not assumed by fixture success.

tickets.title: Acquire permitted open papers as inspectable Source Documents
tickets.deliver: A researcher explicitly selects an eligible open copy, sees its permissions and acquisition outcome, and obtains the same versioned evidence inspection used for private uploads.
criteria: Resolve configured source locations and verified permitted-use basis for the specific copy. Unknown or incompatible permissions keep metadata/permitted abstracts/source links available and explain why automatic full text is unavailable.

Fetch only configured allowed HTTPS source hosts with bounded redirects, private-network/DNS protections, response type/size/page limits and stored acquisition provenance. A PDF URL alone does not authorize retention or model processing.

Route metered download attempts and permitted caching through the shared reservation/usage limits. Confirm selected papers before the 20-document limit, label skipped/throttled copies, and prevent one source consuming a hidden expanded budget.
Hand verified content to the existing parser/anchor flow without silently replacing another source version or researcher corrections. Cache reuse respects permissions and input/version identity.
Use the same project ownership, cancellation/tombstone/cleanup and signed-access policy as private uploads; no public redistribution or arbitrary model-chosen fetching.

Fixture-backed API/browser checks cover allowed copy, missing permissions, unavailable full text, redirect/private-network attack, content mismatch, quota exhaustion, repeated fetch and late response after deletion. Record live accepted license/sample routes before enabling automatic retrieval.

tickets.title: Author Candidate Gaps with traceable evidence and feasibility
tickets.deliver: A researcher can create, revise, compare and reject a Candidate Gap manually from included project evidence, even when no model provider or paid budget is available.
criteria: Persist the candidate question/scope/type, contribution/significance, explained relevance/evidence-strength/feasibility, assumptions, coverage limits and validation next step. Use the spec gap types and no novelty percentage.

Attach supporting/contrary/ambiguous factual claims to owned included paper and anchor revisions; author limitations, searched-set absence and inference/hypothesis are distinct labels. Reject nonexistent/cross-project IDs and invalid positive support.

Capture the immutable snapshot/screening/brief/evidence input footprint. Known retracted/withdrawn work cannot count as ordinary positive support; source updates/edits mark affected candidate evidence for attention without overwriting user work.

Display editable candidates and an evidence inspector with reasons for missing/unverified support. Reject/revise actions retain history. Comparisons may select up to three actual closest-work records; detailed contested review arrives in the counter-search slice.

Feasibility is constraint-checked, provisional or infeasible. Unknown indispensable resources require named assumptions and concrete checks; known unavailable indispensable resources require a credible alternative before an acceptable review.

Manual creation needs no model consent or budget. Preserve optimistic-concurrency behavior, project cleanup, accessible long-content forms and generated-proposal-compatible provenance fields without calling a model.

API/browser fixtures cover supported/unsupported/abstract-only claims, missing and cross-project anchors, known retraction, edited quotations, unknown/impossible constraints, rejected history and revision conflict.

tickets.title: Generate grounded Candidate Gaps within explicit consent and budgets
tickets.deliver: A researcher consents to specified private-content processing, requests zero-to-five anchored candidate proposals, and sees usable results or an honest needs-evidence/failure state without losing manual work.
criteria: Implement the configured OpenAI Responses provider behind the narrow model contract. Pin evaluated model/prompt/schema versions and use stateless bounded extracted-text calls; no provider-hosted files/retrieval, autonomous code, or arbitrary fetching.

Check scoped/versioned consent for every private input category, included source permissions, exact input footprint, active-job limits and paid price/usage reservation before dispatch. Refusal/withdrawal blocks pending calls, not manual review or public-only metadata use.

Enforce zero-to-five proposals, 50,000 aggregate model input tokens, bounded configured output, run/month/global caps, and quota accounting across retries. Record model/config/input hashes/times/usage/validation while redacting private content from operational logs.

Validate schemas, known identifiers, source versions, excerpts/evidence levels and invalid positive support. Valid structure does not establish semantic entailment: all proposals remain unreviewed. Invalid IDs/JSON/quotes yield no adoptable candidate; insufficient evidence may return zero candidates with specific next actions.
Promote validated proposals through the same manual candidate revision/evidence contract. Regeneration creates a separate proposal and never overwrites accepted edits or stale evidence markers.

An ambiguous external outcome stays uncertain/failed with conservative held accounting and no automatic paid replay. User-requested retry gets a new reservation and keeps attempt history; cancellation/revocation/deletion rejects late publication.

API/browser fixtures test consent refusal/withdrawal, unknown pricing, concurrent caps, model refusal, bad schema/IDs/quotes, abstract overreach, prompt injection, no candidates, editing after generation and lost response after dispatch. Generated pilot proposals stay feature-disabled until the later live/scientific gate passes.

tickets.title: Challenge Candidate Gaps with closest work and counter-searches
tickets.deliver: A researcher compares actual closest prior work, runs a targeted search for work that could overturn a candidate, and attaches inspected contrary/supplemental evidence with the search outcome intact.
criteria: Provide task/method/conditions/results/overlap/distinction comparisons for up to three actual relevant works. Evidence levels/anchors qualify every factual comparison; fewer works carries an explicit limitation, never fabricated rows.

Use one-to-three editable concept/synonym/closest-work queries to create a new durable counter-search run and immutable supplemental snapshot using the real connectors and existing budget/provenance controls.

Inspect results using the established library/source/anchor interfaces, including private uploads when needed. Attach selected supplemental evidence explicitly to a candidate revision; retain original snapshots and exclusions.

Record successful/empty/partial/failed attempts and their queries/date/coverage. A failed or empty attempt cannot prove no prior work; stale/cache/failure limitations require assessment. Merely running an unrelated search does not alter candidate/review footprints.
Replacing a closest-work suggestion records a researcher rationale. Previously authored factual comparisons cannot silently switch to newer paper text or ignore a known correction/retraction.

API/browser checks show a seeded decisive counterexample, fewer-than-three works, successful and partial/failed counter-search, exact version relationships, ownership, budget stop and reopening an interrupted review. No model generation dependency is required; manual candidates must work here.

tickets.title: Review and adopt a versioned Research Question
tickets.deliver: A researcher completes a defensible Gap Review and adopts one active Research Question, preserving rationale, provisional constraints, prior question revisions and stale-evidence recovery.
criteria: Persist the exact candidate/brief/snapshot/screening/supplemental/comparison/anchor footprint and required significance, feasibility, assumptions, limitations, claim-inspection, counter-search assessment, contrary-evidence assessment and accept/revise/reject decision.

Finishing a review requires at least one completed counter-search attempt; failures/partial coverage require named acknowledgement and cannot establish absence. Important factual claims must be inspected and supported, removed, or explicitly reclassified as hypotheses. Invalid positive support/structural defects block acceptance.

Known indispensable unavailable resources block acceptance without a revised credible alternative. Unknown critical constraints can support only a explicitly provisional reviewed/adopted question with named resource checks and mitigation steps.

Adoption is atomic and ownership/revision-checked, creates an immutable question revision and allows exactly one current question per project. Store question/scope/intended contribution/rationale/limitations and all evidence links; no action certifies novelty.

Candidate, brief, screening, source/anchor or relevant publication-status changes flag affected reviews/current questions for revalidation. Attaching/promoting relevant supplemental evidence changes the footprint; unrelated search alone does not. Old work remains readable; stale reviews cannot support a new adoption.

Re-reviewing after evidence changes or changing direction creates new review/question revisions rather than erasing the original. Expected revisions prevent tab/worker overwrite and retain unsaved input for compare/reload.

API/browser fixtures cover missing rationale/claims, rejected/revised review, contrary evidence, fewer closest works, failed counter-search acknowledgement, stale edits/status, unknown/impossible constraints, cross-project adoption, racing adoptions and previous-question history.

The manual evidence-to-question workflow is now demoable without model generation or automated open fetching. Register review/question cleanup and a stable reviewed-question interface for later research-plan slices; do not add plan/experiment/manuscript tables.

tickets.title: Delete and archive complete research investigations safely
tickets.deliver: A researcher archives/unarchives or deletes an investigation containing real searches, private sources, generated proposals, reviews and questions, and can inspect honest cleanup/recovery states without late content restoration.
criteria: Consolidate the lifecycle hooks introduced with each artifact: immediate tombstone/access/signing/publication denial, archive read-only behavior, cancellation of jobs, owned relational/text/object cleanup and retained public bibliographic facts.

Deletion/revocation races are tested against each actual pipeline, including a download, parsing worker and uncertain model call. In-flight paid usage is reconciled without retaining deleted research content; no late result recreates a project or anchor.

Private cleanup is idempotent/retryable and completes within 24 hours under healthy dependencies, with visible failed/pending operator diagnostics and no research content in logs. Abandoned uploads are reclaimed on the established schedule.

Signed URLs have at most five-minute validity; explain that existing URLs may remain usable until expiry or object removal. Disclose actual deployed backup expiry and external retention separately instead of promising universal instant erasure.

Provide researcher confirmation, deleting/pending-cleanup states, archive restore and operational cleanup reporting. API/browser checks deny guessed former IDs and new URLs immediately, exercise retries/foreign-account deletion and verify actual private files/text are removed.

Do not postpone basic deletion safety until this ticket: each earlier artifact already registers cleanup and checks tombstones. This slice demonstrates and completes the full multi-artifact lifecycle once all pipelines exist.

tickets.title: Resume a guided investigation from its persisted evidence state
tickets.deliver: A returning researcher opens a project overview, sees the current question or exact next evidence/review action, and resumes their investigation across pages, tabs and interrupted sessions.
criteria: Provide a typed ownership-checked overview/read model derived from saved briefs, snapshots, source/anchor review, candidates, counter-searches, reviews, current question, job state and budget/consent limitations. Do not invent a persisted linear stage that loses branching history.

The overview links to complete-brief, review-scope, inspect-search, obtain-evidence, review-candidate, challenge-gap, resolve-stale/unsupported-claim or adopt-question actions. Provisional resource checks and named source/coverage limitations remain visible on the current question.

Project list/overview, Literature, Gaps and Question views share usable navigation, focus and unsaved-edit protection; no future Plan/Experiments/Manuscript dead links. Manual workflow still works when model/provider/consent/budget is unavailable.

Reopening, session renewal, browser focus/reconnect and worker completion refetch persisted state without duplicate paid submission or overwriting edits. Archived/deleting and cleanup states use the established lifecycle/read contracts.

Complete the small Playwright end-to-end brief-to-reviewed-question journey plus stale/partial/empty/insufficient-evidence/budget-stop recovery at 360px and 1280px. Check keyboard/focus/status announcements and long excerpt/comparison readability.

API tests verify the read model reflects independent artifact changes, racing revisions, unrelated searches and ownership without exposing private source text in generic lists. This feature can ship on the manual question workflow without blocking on live model enablement.

tickets.title: Verify deployed research integrations and durable worker recovery
tickets.deliver: An operator can inspect repeatable integration-readiness results for the web/API/worker deployment, run controlled smoke checks, and distinguish verified capabilities from missing configuration without enabling unsafe automation.
criteria: Package the existing Vercel web/Hono request services and a separately hosted persistent Node worker against the same PostgreSQL database. Complete the container/config contract already introduced with queued search, with explicit connection limits, health/restart behavior, redacted diagnostics and worker-owned Varlock configuration; request handlers never host a polling loop.

Provide persisted readiness results and an operator-only report for source credentials/terms/quota/pricing, accepted full-text routes and representative PDF anchors, private storage signing/cleanup, transaction/queue recovery, auth invite/revoke/verification/recovery, and local/deployed cookie/origin/routing checks. Results have environment/config version and checked date; missing/failed checks stay visible.

Ordinary fixtures can run the readiness/report workflow without real mail, spending or hosting. Live smoke checks are separate explicit commands/actions; unavailable credentials or approval yield pending, never a fake pass. Protect readiness updates from researchers and unauthorized callers.

Exercise real queue restart, job cancellation/revocation, atomic reservations and deletion against the configured runtime after authorization. Document actual backup-expiry/external-retention settings, database worker/migration routes and failure recovery.

Run relevant TypeScript, read-only Biome, API integration, migration and browser checks and record their evidence. Existing live integrations can be marked verified only from real observations; a fixture-success report must be labelled fixture-only.

Provide an operator runbook for configuration, controlled checks, connectivity limits, mail/provider/storage outages, disable/rollback and recovery. This ticket delivers the deployment/readiness workflow; final pilot/model enablement waits for the separate scientific report and final gate.

tickets.title: Evaluate raw and reviewed Candidate Gaps against expert-labelled cases
tickets.deliver: An operator and experienced reviewer can evaluate approximately twenty empirical-ML cases, inspect raw versus corrected proposals and record scientific readiness without mistaking curated edits for model reliability.
criteria: Provide a repeatable evaluation workflow and inspectable persisted report over permitted test cases containing closest/contrary work, supported/unsupported claims, stale evidence and constrained feasibility. Reuse real discovery/generation/review/adoption contracts with fixtures by default and separately authorized live calls.

Preserve raw proposals before researcher correction and score raw/reviewed outputs separately. Record critical fabricated/materially unsupported gap/closest-work claims, concealed decisive counterevidence, knowingly infeasible questions labelled feasible, retrieval outcomes, edits per candidate, review time and explicit case/candidate/claim denominators.

Expert-labelled reference cases and actual expert adjudication are required inputs with provenance/reviewer/date. Missing adjudication is pending; an agent-created fixture or automated structural validator cannot self-certify scientific support. No private researcher content is exposed to an operator by adding this report workflow.

The passing scientific report requires zero critical errors in raw launch output, scoped indexed seeded closest/contrary work found or honestly unavailable with provisional case status, and zero unresolved critical errors after review. Report the chosen fifteen-minute median review target as usability evidence, not an advertised guarantee.

Failed/pending reports keep generated pilot candidates disabled while permitting manual evidence/review work. Evaluate refusal, incomplete-source and insufficient-evidence outcomes as honest states rather than filling a candidate quota. Metered evaluation uses the same consent, quotas and run/project/global caps; no hidden budget bypass.

API/report tests protect raw results from overwrite, distinguish post-correction safety from initial output, reject forged/unauthorized pass records and report denominators/missing review accurately. Provide a small reviewer/runbook workflow for updating cases and re-evaluating changed model/prompt/source versions. This is a scientific enablement gate, not evidence of general research accuracy.

tickets.title: Gate invite-only pilot enablement on verified readiness reports
tickets.deliver: An operator sees which pilot capabilities are eligible and can enable only those with current integration and scientific readiness, while researchers retain an honest manual path when automation is disabled.
criteria: Combine versioned integration and scientific reports into an operator-only enablement/readiness view and backend-enforced feature gates. Model/prompt/provider/runtime/terms changes relevant to a capability invalidate its evidence until rechecked; never enable a failing or missing capability from a UI-only switch.

Model generation requires both a verified live integration report and an adjudicated passing scientific report; automatic full-text retrieval requires its verified live permissions/storage/parser checks. A manual-only pilot remains possible with verified auth/source/storage readiness and accurate limitations.

Record operator action, actual environment, report versions and enabled capabilities. External credentials, live checks, expert adjudication and deployment approval remain explicit prerequisites; missing inputs leave gates pending without fabricated sign-off.

Test unauthorized toggles, stale/failed/missing report combinations, generation dispatch races during disablement, manual fallback and one full invited research-brief-to-adopted-question browser journey. Demonstrate operator invite/revoke, recovery, job restart and content cleanup from linked reports before live pilot designation.

Publish the five-to-ten-researcher pilot runbook with the experienced reviewer, incident/disable/recovery procedures, correction/time-to-reviewed-question and repeat-use observations. No billing, automatic publication or mobile workflow is introduced.

Implementation completion records all required static/integration/browser checks. Live-ready status additionally requires genuine external readiness; fixture-only completion is displayed as development readiness. No production deployment, real-user email, spending or server startup happens as a side effect of ordinary checks.

review_notes: Starter inspection and typecheck completed; representative non-mutating formatting check failed.
Independent review: established shared archived-project mutation guard and split operational integration readiness, scientific evaluation and final pilot gates.
User delegated decisions without a questionnaire; publishing authorization follows the requested to-tickets step.
